title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Architecture (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Architecture (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: The perceptions of our brain on the environment are depending upon the psychological needs and ability to interpret or understanding. The choice of wall colors can make a space seem larger or smaller than it actual. Therefore, which one of the following colors mismatched with the psychological interpretations and meanings?
questions.explanation: Orange is primarily associated with warmth, enthusiasm, creativity, and stimulation - not with unambiguousness (clarity/certainty) as suggested in the option. While orange does convey warmth or 'hotness', the term 'unambiguousness' is incorrectly associated with this color in architectural color psychology.

questions.questionText: In the building systems heat transfer by means of contact of two bodies in collision is called _____
questions.explanation: Conduction is the process of heat transfer through direct contact.

questions.questionText: In both the heating and cooling of buildings, a major design decision is the choice of the energy-transfer medium. What are the most common alternatives of energy-transfer medium?
questions.explanation: Air and water are the most common energy-transfer mediums in building systems.

questions.questionText: What are the advantages of using electric lighting instead of using daylighting in the buildings?
options: It is the ease and flexibility it allowable
Its ability to satisfy biological and human needs
It is connecting with natural, satisfies psychological rhythms
It can also reduce the heating and cooling energy consumption
questions.explanation: Electric lighting provides ease and flexibility in design and usage.

questions.questionText: In northern latitudes, where winter days are short, depression is more common in the winter than in the summer. This illness is now called __________
questions.explanation: Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a type of depression that occurs at a specific time of year, usually in winter.

questions.questionText: What are the main sources of daylight which can enters through a window?
questions.explanation: All listed options are sources of daylight that can enter through a window.

questions.questionText: What are the horizontal members in a building?
questions.explanation: Slabs, beams, and lintels are all horizontal structural members in a building.

questions.questionText: The primary concept of working triangle in a kitchen is based on:
questions.explanation: The working triangle concept is based on the proximity of the three main work areas in the kitchen.

questions.questionText: At what stage should you consider Site Analysis?
options: At the very onset, during the Pre-Design stage
Anytime during the Design Development Stage
questions.explanation: Site analysis should be considered at the very onset, during the Pre-Design stage.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the plan which gives location with respect to neighborhood boundary?
questions.explanation: A key plan shows the location of a building or site in relation to its larger context, including neighborhood boundaries. A site plan focuses on the specific site rather than its relationship to the surrounding neighborhood.

questions.questionText: It is the vertical or horizontal axis of the mass.
questions.explanation: Direction refers to the vertical or horizontal axis of a mass.

questions.questionText: What is the name of horizontally sliced building viewed from top?
questions.explanation: A plan is a horizontal slice of a building viewed from above.

questions.questionText: A covering used to conceal the floor above or the roof.
questions.explanation: Ceilings are coverings that conceal the floor above or the roof.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the important advantage of orientation of building?
questions.explanation: Proper orientation can significantly reduce energy bills.

questions.questionText: It is a need to answer the desire to make something which is not strictly utilitarian.
questions.explanation: Aesthetics refers to the desire to create something beautiful beyond utility.

questions.questionText: It is the beginning of the building and the foundation upon which the scheme of the structure rests.
questions.explanation: The idea or concept is the beginning of any building project and the foundation upon which the entire scheme rests. The plan is a documentation of this idea, but the initial concept comes first.

questions.questionText: A name given to a visual measure of design based upon the proportion of the human body and on mathematics.
questions.explanation: The modular system is based on human proportions and mathematical principles.

questions.questionText: An applied science concerned with the characteristics of people that need to be considered in the design of devices and systems in order that people and things will interact effectively and safely.
questions.explanation: Ergonomics focuses on designing systems that fit human needs.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the total floor area inclusive of all the to the area of the plot on which building stands are
questions.explanation: This question refers to Floor Area Ratio (FAR) or Floor Space Index (FSI), which is the ratio of a building's total floor area to the size of the plot. The built-up area represents this total floor area in relation to the plot.

questions.questionText: Which of the below utility cannot be provided underneath a floor?
questions.explanation: Gas lines are typically not installed underneath floors for safety reasons. Unlike other utilities, gas leaks pose serious explosion and fire hazards if trapped under floors. Building codes generally restrict placing gas lines in enclosed spaces where leaks can't be easily detected or where gas can accumulate.

questions.questionText: A plan is conventionally Cut at the
questions.explanation: Plans are conventionally cut at the window sill level.

questions.questionText: Which of the followings is NOT a reason for architects and interior designers to use bubble diagrams?
options: To create aesthetic buildings and interior spaces
To create functional buildings and interior spaces
questions.explanation: Bubble diagrams are not primarily used for aesthetic purposes.

questions.questionText: It is the simplest structural element.
questions.explanation: The wall is considered the simplest structural element.

questions.questionText: Represented by a building which meets in a satisfactory manner the requirement of logical function, solid construction and beautiful composition.
questions.explanation: Architecture is defined by its ability to meet functional, structural, and aesthetic requirements.

questions.questionText: An architectural element which serves as a screen to deflect side air current, the sun's rays or to abstract vision.
questions.explanation: A baffle is used to deflect air currents and sunlight.

questions.questionText: A phenomenon wherein drawings consisting of black lines are recognized as representing an object is quickly recognized by the observer.
questions.explanation: Figure ground refers to the relationship between objects and their background.

questions.questionText: It is a quality of character of architecture expressive of definitive conceptions...
questions.explanation: Style refers to the distinctive characteristics of architecture.

questions.questionText: If you were invited as an Engineer to prepare a design for this client what is your primary step?
questions.explanation: Identifying needs is the first step in preparing a design.

questions.questionText: Where will be the proper location for the design the medical store room?
options: Adjacent to the dining and living room
questions.explanation: The medical store room should be located between the office and treatment room for efficiency.

questions.questionText: Which rooms you are going to be designed in proximity to one another?
questions.explanation: All listed options represent rooms that should be designed in proximity for functional flow.

questions.questionText: After completing the design phase what you are going to do to start construction works?
options: Site visit and review the report
questions.explanation: Setting out the building layout is the next step after the design phase.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is NOT basic element of design?
questions.explanation: Balance is a principle of design, not a basic element.

questions.questionText: Which one is different?
questions.explanation: Form and shape are distinct from the other concepts which relate to design principles.

questions.questionText: Through the design, the architect must protect the of the general public and the users of the buildings.
questions.explanation: Architects must protect health, welfare, and safety in their designs.

questions.questionText: A company licensed to perform certain types of construction activities responsible for the execution, supervision and overall coordination of a project is
questions.explanation: A contractor is responsible for the execution and coordination of construction projects.

questions.questionText: Represents emotion and allows objects to stand out from the background
questions.explanation: Color is used to evoke emotions and create contrast in design.

questions.questionText: According to the very earliest surveying on the subject of good buildings satisfy three principles: Vitruvius said that architecture was a building that incorporated:
questions.explanation: All listed principles are essential to good architecture according to Vitruvius.

questions.questionText: The education of the architect mainly focusing on the following items
options: Humanities, Arts, and Science and Engineering
questions.explanation: Architectural education encompasses a broad range of disciplines.

questions.questionText: What are the THREE COMPONENTS of architecture used to treat the buildings Aesthetic qualities and or appearance of the whole compositions?
options: Size and shape, treatment, and orientation
Place – spaces, path – spaces, and transition – spaces
questions.explanation: Size and shape, treatment, and orientation are key components in architectural aesthetics.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements are true about general design definition?
options: Design is both a process & a product
The process of designing and product that is designed
Design is an activity aiming at the production of a plan of action
The organization of parts into a coherent whole a creative endeavor to solve a problem
questions.explanation: All statements accurately describe aspects of design.

questions.questionText: The Gestalt principles are a set of laws arising from 1920s' psychology, describing ______
options: Seeing objects by grouping similar elements
All of the above except D
questions.explanation: Gestalt principles focus on how we perceive and organize visual elements.

questions.questionText: What are the spatial relationships of space in architecture?
options: Space within spaces, Interlocking spaces, and Adjacent spaces
Spaces linked by a common space and transition spaces
questions.explanation: The spatial relationships in architecture include all the mentioned types: space within spaces, interlocking spaces, adjacent spaces, spaces linked by a common space, transition spaces, and courtyard spaces. These different relationships create the organizational structure of architectural space.

questions.questionText: From the listed chooses which one is not Spatial organizations principles of forms and spaces in architecture.
questions.explanation: Inclined organization is not a recognized principle of spatial organization.

questions.questionText: What are the three components of architecture for creating meaningful abstract and architectural 3D forms?
options: Size and shape, treatment and orientation
Size and shape, treatment and organization
Form and shape, treatment and organization
Form and size, treatment and organization
questions.explanation: Size and shape, treatment, and orientation are essential for creating meaningful forms.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is NOT basic element of design?
questions.explanation: Balance is a principle of design, not a basic element.

questions.questionText: Which one is cool color or representing relaxing emotions for human beings?
questions.explanation: Blue is considered a cool color that evokes relaxation.

questions.questionText: Any structure ≠ Architecture
questions.explanation: The statement 'Any structure ≠ Architecture' is true. While all architecture involves structures, not all structures qualify as architecture. Architecture specifically involves intentional design considerations including aesthetics, function, cultural context, and human experience, whereas many structures are purely utilitarian or functional without these considerations.

questions.questionText: What is the graphical language the designers use?
questions.explanation: Designers use various graphical languages, excluding paint.

questions.questionText: All are the functional or aesthetic purpose of texture except one
questions.explanation: All of the listed options are actually valid functional or aesthetic purposes of texture in architecture. Textures are used for acoustical treatment (sound absorption/reflection), exterior rendering (visual interest), and preventing accidents on slippery surfaces (grip/traction). None is incorrect.

questions.questionText: Which one following are NOT the elements of design?
questions.explanation: The answer is incorrect. Plane is actually considered a basic element of design along with point, line, and volume. It would have been correct if the option was a design principle (like balance, rhythm, emphasis) rather than an element.

questions.questionText: Acoustical design requirements always should be considered during
questions.explanation: Acoustical design should be integrated from the earliest stages of the design process.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following are the main factors responsible for making the microclimate deviate from the macro-climate:
options: Elevation above sea level and Form of land
Size, shape, and proximity of bodies of water
questions.explanation: All listed factors can influence microclimates.

questions.questionText: What are the climatic factors must be considered in early stages of architectural design process?
questions.explanation: Climatic zones and wind directions are critical factors in early design stages.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of a design concept?
options: To provide a basis for a design project
To ensure a design meets aesthetic standards
To create a solution to a problem
To make a design project stand out
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a design concept is to provide a foundational basis for the project.

questions.questionText: What type of presentation style works best when presenting design ideas?
questions.explanation: Visual presentation styles are most effective for conveying design ideas.

questions.questionText: ______________ refers to the effect produced by deriving the maximum benefits from the minimum dimensions of a room.
questions.explanation: Roominess refers to maximizing benefits from minimal space.

questions.questionText: How do you develop an architectural program?
options: Establish goals, objectives and Identify strategies.
Gather relevant information and determine quantitative requirements.
questions.explanation: All steps are essential in developing a comprehensive architectural program.

questions.questionText: Which aspect of architecture involves the observation, analysis and understanding of the connections between People, activity and Place.
questions.explanation: The social aspect of architecture focuses on the interactions between people and their environments.

questions.questionText: Main purpose of building envelops [facade'] is to act as____________
questions.explanation: Building envelopes serve functional, psychological, and aesthetic purposes.

questions.questionText: How does context affect architectural space?
questions.explanation: Context influences architectural space in multiple ways.

questions.questionText: Which of the lines is a thin continuous line with the ends terminating in arrowheads and is enclosed by extension lines, outlines or centre lines?
questions.explanation: A dimension line is used to indicate measurements in drawings.

questions.questionText: How many pairs of parallel lines are there in a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has no pairs of parallel lines.

questions.questionText: An egg is placed vertical to horizontal plane the top view will be ______________
questions.explanation: The top view of an egg placed vertically will appear as a circle.

questions.questionText: A circular surface plane is making 30 degrees with both H.P and V.P. The front view will be ___ ____________
questions.explanation: The front view of a circular surface at an angle will appear as an ellipse.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements are wrongly describing about equilibrium temperature of a surface
options: Heating, cooling, and lighting of buildings requires a fair amount of knowledge of the behavior of radiant energy.
Materials vary in the way they emit and absorb radiant energy
Black has a much higher equilibrium temperature than white because it has a much higher absorptance factor
Black is not the ideal collector of radiant energy because of its high emissivity.
questions.explanation: None of the statements are wrong; they all accurately describe equilibrium temperature.

questions.questionText: Which of the following type of foundation is used for the construction of building on black cotton soil?
questions.explanation: Mat foundations are suitable for black cotton soil due to their load distribution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following term is used to indicate the art of building the structures in stones?
questions.explanation: Masonry refers to the art of constructing structures from stones.

questions.questionText: Baluster in a stair is the _________ member supporting _________
questions.explanation: Balusters are vertical members that support the handrail.

questions.questionText: A wooden piece provided at the Ridge line of a sloping roof is known as the ____________
questions.explanation: The ridge is the horizontal line at the top of a sloping roof.

questions.questionText: Low heat cement is used in
questions.explanation: Low heat cement is used in thick structures to minimize heat generation during curing.

questions.questionText: The main ingredients of Portland cement are
questions.explanation: Portland cement is primarily made from lime and silica.

questions.questionText: The type of bond in which every course contains both headers and stretchers, is called
questions.explanation: Flemish bond alternates headers and stretchers in each course.

questions.questionText: The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a considerable depth from earth's surface are called
questions.explanation: Plutonic rocks form from magma cooling slowly beneath the Earth's surface.

questions.questionText: Cast iron contains carbon approximately
questions.explanation: Cast iron typically contains 1.5% to 5.5% carbon.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is termed as an action of pull or push of a body at rest or motion?
questions.explanation: Force is defined as a push or pull acting on an object.

questions.questionText: Which of the following contains moving parts?
questions.explanation: Machines are designed to contain moving parts for operation.

questions.questionText: What does Newton's third law states?
options: The rate of change of momentum is equal to the force applied
For every reaction, there is an opposite reaction
The body tends to be rotated if the force is applied tangentially
The body is rest until a force is applied
questions.explanation: Newton's third law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. The answer option is slightly incorrect in wording - it should be 'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction' rather than 'For every reaction, there is an opposite reaction.'

questions.questionText: What is the factor of safety?
options: The ratio of stress to strain
The ratio of permissible stress to the ultimate stress
The ratio of ultimate stress to the permissible stress
The ratio of longitudinal strain to stress
questions.explanation: The factor of safety is defined as the ratio of ultimate stress to permissible stress.

questions.questionText: The unit of force in S.I. unit is?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of force is the Newton.

questions.questionText: Shear force is unbalanced _____ to the left or right of the section.
questions.explanation: Shear force is typically considered as a vertical force acting on a section.

questions.questionText: A simple support offers only _______ reaction normal to the axis of the beam.
questions.explanation: A simple support provides a vertical reaction force.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not the fundamental laws that architecture must obey to be considered
questions.explanation: Harmony with nature is not considered a fundamental law of architecture.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not ergonometric consideration.
questions.explanation: Privacy factor is not a primary ergonomic consideration.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not directly define the Space protagonist architectural consideration?
options: Painting functions in two dimensions, even if it can suggest three or four.
poem is something more than just a sum of fine verses, architecture is also something more than just a sum of beautiful walls.
questions.explanation: Space is the primary protagonist in architecture, while aesthetic quality, though important, is secondary to spatial considerations. Architecture is fundamentally about the creation and manipulation of space, whereas aesthetic quality relates to the visual and sensory experience of that space.

questions.questionText: Dominance and contrast can be achieved by
questions.explanation: Dominance and contrast in design can be effectively achieved through organization and arrangement.

questions.questionText: All are considered as forcing factors of architectural design as creativity except…?
options: Program (the analysis of the project purpose)
questions.explanation: Budget is a constraint rather than a forcing factor of creativity in architectural design.

questions.questionText: All are Pragmatic Approaches to deriving design idea except…?
options: Use of an established form/ symbol/ pattern
questions.explanation: Using established forms/symbols/patterns is considered a canonic or iconic approach to design, not a pragmatic one. Pragmatic approaches are rooted in practical, functional solutions rather than established aesthetic or symbolic references. Pragmatic design is driven by utility, material availability, and experimentation (trial and error).

questions.questionText: A design idea deriving approach Derived from applied rules, proportioning systems Prescription
questions.explanation: Canonic approaches are based on established rules and proportioning systems.

questions.questionText: Art Nouveau was a new art form inspired by
questions.explanation: Art Nouveau is often referred to as 'total art' due to its integration of various art forms.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not Characteristics of Cubism
questions.explanation: The Fauve color palette is not a characteristic of Cubism.

questions.questionText: What are the basic elements for balanced professional architectural skills?
questions.explanation: Balanced professional architectural skills encompass design, technology, and management.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the type of contract, according to the PPA Guidelines?
questions.explanation: Both Lump Sum and Time-based contracts are recognized types according to PPA Guidelines.

questions.questionText: According to the Ethiopian building proclamation No. 62/2009, this refers to a building that is structurally unsafe or constitute a special fire hazard or health.
questions.explanation: A dangerous building is defined as one that poses structural or health risks.

questions.questionText: With respect to responsibilities to colleagues and subordinates, which of the following is unethical practice for the architects?
options: Affixes signature to plans prepared by another person's or entities.
Refrains from associating with any enterprise of doubtful character
Refrains from participating at competitions where he has involvement in its programs
questions.explanation: Affixing a signature to plans not prepared by oneself is considered unethical.

questions.questionText: Participants in an architectural design competition should be
questions.explanation: Only registered architects are eligible to participate in architectural design competitions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following examples is NOT preferred in good specifications of writing?
options: Avoid complicated sentences which create ambiguity
Main sentence structure in simple declarative statements
Choose words/items that are plain and well-understood to convey information
questions.explanation: Using long sentences can create ambiguity and is not preferred in specifications.

questions.questionText: Who approves the overall design and position of a building?
questions.explanation: The architect is responsible for approving the overall design and position of a building.

questions.questionText: ______ is a preferred sampling method for the population with finite size.
questions.explanation: Systematic sampling is a preferred method for populations with finite size because it ensures a uniform selection process.

questions.questionText: ______ is a process of measuring or scaling dimensions from drawings and recording all dimensions in an easily understood format.
questions.explanation: Taking Off is the process of measuring dimensions from drawings and recording them in a structured format.

questions.questionText: ______ describe the construction supervision, construction project management including checking of payment certificates prepared by contractor and interpretation of contract document.
questions.explanation: Implementation services include construction supervision, project management, and contract document interpretation.
